body.title: Wire the src/deploy/ chain.ts + runner scaffold (register<Stage> registrar seam)
body.summary: Create src/deploy/chain.ts plus a runner-scaffold index.ts + schemas.ts pair, mirroring the src/workflow/runners/<name>/ + src/workflow/chain.ts idiom. chain.ts drives the stage order discover → reuse → topology → {security, scale-HA} → done through handleDeployStep and exposes the register<Stage>Runners() registrar seam (DeployStageRegistrar) that s2–s6 plug stages into without touching chain internals. Because the real s2–s6 stage bodies do not exist yet, s1 proves the ordering over stubbed stage runners emitting deterministic DeploymentContextBundles, per the LLD testStrategy. The security/scale fan-out runs as serial DeployPhase transitions.
acceptanceChecks: src/deploy/chain.ts drives stage order discover → reuse → topology → {security, scale} → done via handleDeployStep, proven in s1 over stubbed stage runners emitting deterministic DeploymentContextBundles, with the security/scale fan-out executed as serial DeployPhase transitions (never Promise.all over a provider).
A runner index.ts exposes a register<Stage>Runners(): void registrar (camelCase) that binds a DeployStageRegistrar into the deploy-step dispatch table, with a paired schemas.ts contract file.

chain-order internals (wiring order, RPC dispatch, state serialization) are private to s1 — downstream stages see only the DeployStepProtocol envelope and DeploymentContextBundle, never the chain internals.
File names follow the sibling idiom (chain.ts / index.ts / schemas.ts) and functions are camelCase per the convention-detect finding.
